result.title: Behaviour analysis for large language model-driven agents
result.comment: Under review by Nature Machine Intelligence
result.summary: Understanding language-agent behaviour requires learning how actions are organised across a trajectory and how this organisation relates to context and outcomes. We propose a general framework that connects data-driven behavioural discovery with analysis and experimental investigation. Categories developed from recorded activity define what is measured. Analyses preserve the behaviours' positions in the process and express their relationships as interpretable hypotheses. Statistical assessment and tests in held-out contexts examine the strength and scope of the evidence. Experiments, including prompt steering, then test how behaviour and outcomes change under deliberately varied conditions. A study of iterative self-reflection illustrates how discovery, dependency learning and prompt comparisons can inform one another. We develop this approach for trajectories of varying length, event order and agent roles, and identify advances in coding, analysis and experimentation needed to support its wider use.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一个通用框架，把数据驱动的行为发现、轨迹内依赖关系的可解释假设、统计评估与干预实验（含 prompt steering）串联起来，分析 LLM agent 轨迹中行为如何组织并与上下文和结果相关，并以迭代自我反思为案例演示。
AI.relevance_reason: 其轨迹级行为标注、统计检验与 prompt 干预流程可能可供核查能否迁移到 LVR 推理轨迹的测量与评估，例如刻画 THINK/LOOK/STOP 模式组织与停止决策的因果作用；但材料未涉及视觉或多模态 latent 状态，联系较间接。
